inventoryMapping.sourceFact: One connected bent tube, short left cap, tall right rim and continuous lower bend.
inventoryMapping.evidence: Actual original and preview pixels plus the four explicit SVG path definitions. No hidden joints, supports, funnels or added components.

inventoryMapping.sourceFact: Continuous dark column with two unequal surfaces and clear upper regions.
inventoryMapping.evidence: Low level y=230 and high level y=510 in upward model coordinates; rendered screen levels 490 and 210. Filled bend is continuous. Mercury and trapped air identities come from both current texts, not the pixel inventory.

inventoryMapping.sourceFact: Two horizontal level guides and one vertical h dimension with opposed endpoint arrowheads.
inventoryMapping.evidence: Guide levels coincide with the liquid surfaces. Arrow endpoints coincide with those levels at x=470; h is clear of the bracket.

scientificInterpretation: The capped short limb contains the fixed air sample above its lower mercury surface; the much taller limb has the atmospheric opening/rim. This is consistent with the historical arrangement in the complete current lesson.

A higher mercury surface on the open side is consistent with trapped-gas absolute pressure exceeding atmospheric pressure by the hydrostatic column difference. The diagram does not claim the difference alone is the gas's absolute pressure.
The single unequal-level state is not confused with the initial equal-level state described in the text.
h is not calibrated. The lesson's 760 millimeter example, pressure doubling and volume halving are not fabricated from pixels or drawn as universal quantitative conclusions.
No temperature-changing process, extra gas inlet, phase transition or experimental operation is depicted.
modernAdditionsDistinct: Smooth U-bend outlines, regular stroke widths and upright h are typography/layout regularizations, not measured source dimensions.
Semantic accentSoft fill replaces the source's solid dark fluid region; ink boundaries and liquid surface strokes retain the material topology.
Clearer cap and rim treatment is consistent with source outlines and text, not an invented labelled component.

visual640.observation: Tube, cap, rim, both clear upper regions, continuous fill, two levels and both h arrowheads are visible and separated. Geometry is comfortably inside the canvas.

inventoryMapping.sourceFact: Two finite solid descending convex curves in the positive quadrant, noncrossing at shared volume.
inventoryMapping.evidence: Original and preview comparison plus current path data and existing hash-bound D174 analytic check; pV constancy is not proved by objectCount. Supplementary inverse-law evidence is essential.

inventoryMapping.sourceFact: t2 > t1 and each curve's right-end label.
inventoryMapping.evidence: Plain mathematical t1/t2 forms preserve source indices; upper curve is t2, lower is t1. The inequality is separate and unobstructed.

scientificInterpretation: Both current texts restrict this illustration to the same fixed gas amount and an ideal-gas model with absolute pressure. Real-gas limitations remain in the text.
Each curve represents a different constant temperature, not a single process in which temperature rises along one curve.

The disclosed analytical construction is p=K/V with K positive and constant separately on each isotherm. For a common positive V, the larger K gives the larger p; this agrees with t2 > t1 and the higher t2 curve.
The internal layout constants are not temperatures, physical pressure readings or a Celsius temperature ratio. The candidate does not display or claim those numbers.
Finite visible endpoints and solid/dashed distinction agree with the source. No curve touches an axis, crosses the other curve, gains an arrowhead, or extends into negative pressure or volume.
There are no source numerical query coordinates or labelled extrema to preserve. Smooth ideal hyperbolas are a disclosed text-justified regularization, not a reconstruction of measured source data.
modernAdditionsDistinct: Uncalibrated exact inverse-law sampling is justified by the current lesson's explicit hyperbola claim. Layout constants and invisible polyline nodes are not source facts or marked gas states.
Uniform strokes and upright plain-text index forms t1/t2 replace the source's hand-printed mathematical styling without adding variables.

One short unlabelled horizontal-axis stroke remains. The independent pixel inventory treated tiny strokes as uncalibrated irregularities; its presence is not accepted as evidence of an interval, numerical value or a queried volume.

visual640.observation: Both complete finite curves, axis arrowheads and all six labels are readable at 640. The two right-end labels are clearly associated with their curves and separated from one another; V and p stay inside the canvas.

answerCulturalSafety.reason: This is the lesson's instructional relationship, not an exercise solution; no marked states, projections, numerical readings or solutions are added.

independentCurrentPathArithmetic.sameVolumeOrdering: For every shared V>0, (K2-K1)/V>0; K values are layout-only, not source readings or temperature ratios.
